q: Goodman's theorem extends the variational principle by showing that for expansive homeomorphisms T of compact metric spaces:
opts: h_top(T) = sup_μ h_μ(T) with the supremum achieved
h_top(T) = max_μ h_μ(T) — the supremum is always achieved (maximum entropy measures exist)
h_top(T) = h_μ(T) for every ergodic μ
exp: Goodman: for expansive homeomorphisms, the variational principle gives a maximum (not just supremum). The maximum entropy measure exists for expansive systems. This includes SFTs (where the Parry measure achieves the maximum) and Axiom A attractors.
